system_overview: A multiprocess parallel implementation of Misra's graph reachability algorithm. Multiple processes concurrently explore a directed graph to compute the set of nodes reachable from a given root node. Each process independently picks frontier nodes, marks them, and adds their successors to the shared frontier one at a time. The module proves that this parallel algorithm implements (refines) the sequential Misra algorithm under a defined refinement mapping.
actors_and_components: A finite set of worker processes that execute concurrently. Each process has local variables tracking its currently selected node and its local set of successors still to be added to the shared frontier. All processes share a global set of marked nodes and a global frontier set. Written in PlusCal with the attached translation.
state_variables: Five state variables: (1) the shared set of marked (visited) nodes, (2) the shared frontier set of nodes to explore, (3) per-process program counters indicating each process's current execution point, (4) per-process local variable holding the node currently being processed, and (5) per-process local set of successor nodes that still need to be added to the frontier.
initial_state: The marked set is empty. The frontier contains only the root node. Each process starts at the beginning of its main loop with its local node set to the root and its local successor set empty.
actions: Three per-process actions at distinct control points. (1) At the loop head: if the frontier is non-empty, pick an arbitrary frontier node and store it locally; if the frontier is empty, the process terminates. (2) At the marking step: if the local node is not yet marked, add it to marked and set the local successor set to all its graph successors; otherwise, remove the local node from the frontier and return to the loop head. (3) At the successor-adding step: if the local successor set is non-empty, pick one node from it, add it to the frontier, and remove it from the local set; when all successors have been added, return to the loop head.
safety_properties: The parallel algorithm refines the sequential Misra algorithm. An inductive invariant establishes type correctness and two key relationships: each process's local successor set is empty except when the process is in the successor-adding phase, and a process's selected node is in the frontier or marked set when the process is at the marking step. The refinement mapping defines the sequential algorithm's frontier as the parallel frontier plus all processes' local successor sets, and the sequential program counter as terminated only when all parallel processes have terminated.
liveness_properties: The algorithm terminates if and only if the set of reachable nodes is finite. When it terminates, the marked set equals exactly the set of nodes reachable from the root. Weak fairness is assumed for each process.
additional_assumptions: The root is a valid graph node. The process set is non-empty and finite. A process may observe the frontier as empty and terminate before all reachable nodes are found, but correctness is maintained because at least one process will continue running until the computation is complete. In practice, the frontier emptiness test can be implemented to reduce premature termination.
